label: input token k during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: Fires on every original-phase step whose input is the letter k (dev precision 1.00, recall 0.999), and on nothing else. Activation mass is 100% original phase. It never fires at the <DEL> step and fires essentially never in the copy phase (92 stray steps in the dev split), even when k is fed back as input there. Magnitude is largest when k comes early (t=0..3 holds most of the mass; the top examples are k at t=2 after a repeated pair, at 1.00 of max) and drops at later positions (k at t>=6 in the lowest quartile, about 0.35-0.6 of max). A repeated k scores lower than the first k (in_first=0 still fires, but more weakly, e.g. 0.86 or 0.57 of the first). The feature does not depend on neighbouring tokens, L, or the digit count beyond these small effects.

issues: Only minor nuance: the 97 stray copy-phase activations on test are k fed back as input at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, e.g. 'k n c <DEL> [k:0.00]'). Their activations are about 0.00-0.03 of max and they hold 0.0% of the activation mass. This is negligible and does not count as a systematic counterexample class.
Test: precision 1.0, recall 0.9991, F1 0.9996, mass recall 0.99998, 0 false positives. The phase claims check out: zero activations at the <DEL> step, and the copy phase holds 0.000 of the mass.

Repeated k still fires: the predicate restricted to in_first==0 has precision 1.0 (10097 steps). The claim that repeats fire 'more weakly' could not be tested directly with score, but it does not affect the predicate.

Position decay checks out: t=0..3 each hold about 16-20% of the mass, and the share falls for t>=4. Per-step firing rate is flat across orig_idx and L, so the falling mass at later t partly comes from fewer sequences being that long.
